# Shadow CPI: Devpost write-up

> Track: **Best Apps and Agents**. Bonus: Best Use of Tavily. Every number below is filled from the results files by
> `python tools/sync_doc_numbers.py`; edit `docs/templates/devpost.md`, not this file.

## Subtitle
Time-locked web evidence for AI backtests on Tavily: we measured how the future leaks in, shipped a fix under which we
detected 0 of 42 leaking cases, and use it to seal a monthly India inflation forecast.

Shadow CPI is one product: web evidence you can trust as of a date. **Tavily Search** (with `start_date`/`end_date` and
`filter_by_published_date`) finds pages inside the time lock, and **Tavily Extract** reads each page. **NVIDIA Nemotron
Nano** is the yes/no gatekeeper that screens pages, and **NVIDIA Nemotron Super** cites the exact numbered line for each
price; both run on **Nebius Token Factory**. Code checks each number on the page, computes the CPI estimate, and seals it
before the government publishes.

## Headline
<!-- headline:start -->
0 of 42 cases detected leaking with Tavily's dates + filter, across a pilot and a pre-registered replication (Wilson 0–8%); with no dates, 9 of 20 and 14 of 22 leaked.
Reuse: `timelocked_search`, `extract_as_of`, Colab leak check.
<!-- headline:end -->

## Tagline
An AI agent that searches the past without cheating: it uses Tavily inside a time lock it cannot move, checks every
quote on its source page, and seals India's inflation forecast before the government publishes it.

In the forecast pipeline, NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory screens pages and cites quotes; code checks each cited number on the page.

## Short description
<!-- short:start -->
Can a search engine keep the past in the past? We measured Tavily's date controls on 20 replay cases
(pilot, pre-registered). With no dates, 9 of 20 cases kept a confirmed leak, a page dated after
the cutoff with no archive copy before it (Wilson 95% 26–66%; 10 of 20
after retrying 11 failed archive lookups); with `start_date`/`end_date` and
`filter_by_published_date`, 0 of 20 detected (0–16%). The cost: the filter dropped
12 of 40 pieces of valid evidence (initial pass). Dates select pages, not versions. Shadow CPI puts this to work: an AI agent searches with Tavily
inside a time lock, checks each quote against the extracted page with NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory, lets
code compute India's October 2026 inflation nowcast, and seals it before the Ministry of Statistics publishes on
12 Nov.
<!-- short:end -->

## The leak, measured
- **Main result (date test, a pilot; the pre-registered initial pass):** no dates, 9 of 20
  cases leaked (Wilson 95% 26–66%); `start_date`/`end_date` + `filter_by_published_date`,
  0 of 20 detected (0–16%). Update: 10 of 20
  (30–70%) and 0 of 20 detected (0–16%) after retrying the
  11 archive lookups that had failed; the retry only re-ran those lookups, with the same labelling rules.
- **Dates or filter?** Explicit date windows already gave 0 of 20 detected (`start_date`/`end_date` only,
  Wilson 0–16%); the filter additionally drops undated pages (the dates-only search returned
  0 undated of 58 results here).
- **What a leak is.** A case leaks when at least one result the search kept is a confirmed leak, which
  `v2/DATE_TEST_PREREG.md` defines as: "**Confirmed leak (L):** independent version evidence only: the Wayback Machine CDX API (a logged direct download, the same exception as MoSPI) lists **no capture on or before the cutoff**, its first capture is after the cutoff, **and** Tavily's published date or the date in the address is after the cutoff." The finance check's rule differs
  (`v2/FINANCE_PREREG.md`, as amended): "**Confirmed leak:** states the outcome **and** Wayback-confirmed (no capture on or before the cutoff, first capture after it, and Tavily's or the address's date after the cutoff)." Its counts are reported apart and never added to the
  date test's. No-dates counts are lower bounds: a page the Wayback Machine never captured cannot be confirmed
  (absence from Wayback is not proof the page did not exist).
- **Replication and statistics:** 14 of 22 with no dates, 0 of 22
  detected with dates + filter (pre-registered); pooled 0 of 42 detected, rule of three below
  7.1%; exact McNemar p = 0.0039 (date test), 0.00012 (replication), 2.4e-07 (pooled)
  (post-hoc, not pre-registered, `results/posthoc_stats.md`). Without the cache-served replication responses: 11
  of 19 and 0 of 19 detected (the logged addendum).
- **The cost (the measured cost of the strict setting):** the filter dropped 12 of the date test's 40 pieces of valid evidence
  (initial pass; 20 of 48 after the retry).
- **Date filters select which pages, not which version.** Tavily dated `R196`, a TCS results
  preview, 7 Jul, before its 8 Jul cutoff; the page was updated on 9 Jul with a link to the
  actual result, and Extract returns the updated page. `max_age_hours` controls freshness, not as-of;
  `extract_as_of` fills that gap (demo, n=1).
- **Reuse:** `timelock/`, `mcp/`, `benchmarks/timelock34/`.

## Time-locked search leakage
- **Finance check** (exploratory; Reserve Bank of India (RBI) decisions and company results, its own rule above):
  no dates, 2 of 14 events on the pre-registered initial pass (Wilson 95%
  4–40%); with dates and the filter, 0 of 14 detected (0–22%). Update:
  10 of 14 (45–88%) and 0 of 14 detected
  (0–22%) after the retry (94 lookups had failed).
- **Check P, full page** (exploratory): of 132 pages that passed the date lock, 1 described a later
  event; most later dates were page furniture (43 of 71 flagged pages: date bars, sidebars,
  related links).
- **Check E** (exploratory, `exact_match`): its misses are filter misses, not back-dating (0 of
  8 have a later `published_date`).

## Tavily integration map
Every Tavily endpoint and parameter we use or refuse, what we do with it and why; each row is checked against the code in
`tests/test_sync_doc_numbers.py`.

| Endpoint / parameter | How we use it | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `start_date` / `end_date` (Search) | Every time-locked search sends a window that ends on the cutoff; an `end_date` after the cutoff is refused. | The first lock: Tavily only returns pages dated inside the window. |
| `filter_by_published_date` (Search) | Always on inside the time lock; it cannot be switched off there. The date test also ran it off, to measure it. | Also removes results with no detectable date; we measured what that costs. |
| `include_published_date` (Search) | Set on the Try it page, the Leak demo's live mode and the MCP search tool, so each result carries Tavily's date; code then re-checks every date and labels the result safe, date flag or leak. | A date is Tavily's estimate, so code does not take it on trust. |
| `/extract` | Reads each page the pipeline cites. The model returns a line number; code copies that line from the Extract output and checks the number is in it. `extract_as_of` pairs it with Wayback. | Extract returns the page as it is today, so a page edited after the cutoff needs the archive copy. |
| `/map` and `/crawl` | Look for the pages that hold official price lists and tariff orders. | Official sources publish lists, not news. Map returned nothing on several government and dairy sites (a field note). |
| `include_usage` | Sent on every call, by the app's client and by the standalone `timelock` client, and the credits are written to the call log and the credit ledger. | To cap spend per run and report credits per result. |
| `X-Project-ID: shadow-cpi` (header) | Sent on calls to api.tavily.com from the app's HTTP layer. The standalone `timelock` package and the MCP server do not send it, and it is not part of any cache key. | Tavily groups usage by project. |
| MCP tools (`mcp/server.py`) | `search` (the time-locked search), `as_of` (`extract_as_of`) and `check_leaks` (labels results you already have, no Tavily call). They reach Tavily through `timelock.TavilyHTTP` with your own key. | The same lock for any agent. |
| We refuse: `time_range`, `days`, `auto_parameters` | The time lock raises an error before any call if a request carries one of them, or switches the filter off. | They set their own window. `auto_parameters` with no dates reached for the present: 620 of 659 results for past-month queries came from October 2026 (observed once on 22 Oct 2026, not reproduced on 27 Oct 2026). |
| Direct download (outside Tavily) | Official data is fetched directly and logged as service `direct`: the MoSPI API, and the Department of Consumer Affairs price pages, some saved by hand because they sit behind a captcha. `extract_or_download` falls back to a direct download when Extract cannot fetch a page; it is called from one place, the DoCA check in `checks.py`. | Some government sites block Extract. These downloads do not go through Tavily's date filter; the exact-line number check still applies, and every call is logged. |

## What we learned that you wouldn't know
- **Date filters select which pages, not which version of a page.** Tavily dated `R196`, a TCS results
  preview, 7 Jul, before its 8 Jul cutoff; the page was updated on 9 Jul and Extract returns
  the updated page. This is one demonstrated case (`R196`, n=1), not a rate; `extract_as_of` serves the latest
  Wayback copy on or before the cutoff, or nothing.
- **Three questions, and Tavily answers two.** Tavily's best-practices page ([docs.tavily.com](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/best-practices/best-practices-search), "By content freshness") says: "Date filters choose pages by when they were published. max_age_hours sets how recently Tavily must have fetched each page". Those are two questions: when a page was published, and
  how recently Tavily fetched it (the reference describes `max_age_hours` as "The maximum age in hours of Tavily's cached copy of each result."). The third is which
  version of the page existed as of the date, and that is what we measured (`R196`, a demonstration, n=1);
  `extract_as_of` answers it from an archive copy or refuses. We have not tested `max_age_hours`.
- **Explicit dates alone already gave the same count.** `start_date`/`end_date` without the filter gave
  0 of 20 detected (Wilson 0–16%). The filter additionally removes results with no
  detectable date, as Tavily documents; on this sample that changed little, because the dates-only search returned
  0 undated of 58 results, and what the filter costs is counted above.

## What Tavily's docs say vs what we measured
Tavily's API reference, quoted and linked, next to our measurement. Most of what we found is documented behaviour.

| Field | Tavily's docs say (quoted, checked 29 Oct) | What we measured |
|---|---|---|
| `start_date` / `end_date` | ["Will return all results after the specified start date based on publish date or last updated date."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search); ["By default, results with no detectable published date are not removed"](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | Dates select which pages, not which version. `R196`: dated 7 Jul, before its 8 Jul cutoff, updated 9 Jul; Extract returns the updated page. Dates with the filter off (arm B): 0 of 20 detected (Wilson 0–16%) |
| `filter_by_published_date` | ["Results with no detectable published date are also removed."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | Dates + filter: 0 of 20 detected (Wilson 0–16%); replication 0 of 22 detected (0–15%). Measured cost of the strict setting: 12 of 40 pieces of valid evidence dropped (initial pass); undated results 0 with the filter, 8 of 60 with no dates |
| The docs' alternative: `include_published_date` without the filter | ["leave this `false` and set `include_published_date: true` together with a date range instead."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | Our arm B is that setting (dates, `include_published_date` on, filter off): 0 of 20 detected (0–16%), 0 undated of 58 results, 19 of 40 pieces of valid evidence lost (filter on: 12) |
| `published_date` | ["Tavily's best estimate of when the source was published or last updated."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | Later than the page's own date on 4 of 42 distinct date-test pages: documented behaviour (feature request: separate the two dates) |
| `time_range` | ["The time range back from the current date to filter results"](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | `auto_parameters` with no dates chose recent time ranges for past months: 620 of 659 results from October 2026 (observed once on 22 Oct 2026, not reproduced on 27 Oct 2026). Consistent with "back from the current date"; a past month needs `start_date`/`end_date` |
| `max_age_hours` | ["The maximum age in hours of Tavily's cached copy of each result."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | Not sent in our runs. It bounds how fresh Tavily's cached copy is, not which date the copy reflects (freshness, not as-of); the [Extract reference](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/extract) lists no date, cache or crawl-time field. `extract_as_of` fills that gap (demo, n=1: `R196` refused, no archive copy before the 8 Jul cutoff) |
| `language` vs `filter_by_language` | ["Boost search results in a specific language."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search); ["Strictly filter out search results that don't match the `language` parameter, instead of only boosting them in ranking."](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search) | We sent `language` without `filter_by_language` (boost only) on 12 cases: with dates + filter 0 of 12 detected (0–24%); Tamil still returned English pages (post-hoc), as boost-only allows. `filter_by_language` was not tested |

## Search dates do not freeze page content
Date filters select which pages, not which version: a page dated before the cutoff can be updated after it, and
Extract returns the updated page. `max_age_hours` controls freshness, not as-of; `extract_as_of` fills that gap
(demo, n=1). Example (a separate,
post-hoc AI-assisted review (ChatGPT agent); 146 of 283 rows stayed unclear): `R196`, a
TCS results preview, cutoff 8 Jul; Tavily dated it 7 Jul, and the page was updated on
9 Jul with a link to the actual result. 0 of 14 filtered searches in
the finance check returned a result dated after the cutoff; that review found 1 page whose current
version leaks the outcome. What covers the gap, partly: our page-date check (kept 26 of
59 filtered results in the date test; date-test valid evidence lost: 27 of
40 with it (initial pass), 12 with the filter alone; after the retry
35 and 20 of 48); the drift monitor, which re-reads October radar
pages daily (2 runs committed (28 Oct 2026 to 29 Oct 2026 IST), 142 page checks, 31 changes found; in the latest run, 17 of 80 radar pages had changed since they were saved; cited quote still present on 16 of 17; cited number changed on 0 of 17); and Wayback Machine checks, with failed lookups retried and logged
(11 in the date test, 94 in the finance check).

## Who writes the search: model-written fields vs fixed templates, inside a time lock it cannot move
Building on Tavily's dynamic-filtering idea, we let Nemotron write the search fields and tested it on
29 known price changes: code templates (arm A) found 6, Nemotron-written fields (arms B
and C) 2 and 2, `auto_parameters` (arm T) 0; exploratory arm H
(templates + model-chosen fields) 4, and T+dates 2. The model's fields were always
valid (189 of 189; 468 of 468 in arm H), but fixed
templates found more. That is a result about query planning (what Nemotron chose to search for), not about
Tavily, which answered every arm; the likely cause is source choice (arm H differed from A only in domains and
language). An observation: `auto_parameters` with no dates reached for the present, 620 of 659
results from October 2026 (observed once on 22 Oct 2026, not reproduced on 27 Oct 2026); Tavily documents `time_range` as counting back from the current date.
So the model chooses the query, topic, domains and language; code owns the dates.

## Tavily field notes / repro kit: feedback for the Most Valuable Feedback prize
Publishing these measurements was approved by <who, role> on <date> (<link>). Screenshot:
`docs/permission_2026-10-27.png`.

Full notes with request IDs and a one-request repro script each: `docs/tavily_bug_reports.md`. Each is tagged against
Tavily's docs: documented behaviour, doc gap or unexplained.

**Feature requests (2)**
1. **An as-of / crawl-timestamp field** (documented behaviour). Date filters select which pages, not which version:
   `R196` (above) was dated before the cutoff and updated after it, and Extract returns today's copy;
   `max_age_hours` controls freshness, not as-of. `extract_as_of` fills that gap (demo, n=1). *Evidence:*
   `results/timelock34_second_review.json`; the search's request ID is in the notes.
2. **Separate original-publication and last-modified dates** (documented behaviour): `published_date` was later
   than the page's own date on 4 of 42 distinct date-test pages, as the documented definition
   (published or last updated, beta) allows.

**Observations**
- **`auto_parameters` picked a recent `time_range` for queries about a past month** (unexplained; observed once on 22 Oct 2026, not reproduced on 27 Oct 2026):
  with no dates, on 72 searches naming a month in Jan–Sep 2026, 620 of 659
  results came from October 2026. *Evidence:* `v2/ablation/arm_T_*.json`; request IDs in the notes.
- **With explicit dates, the `auto_parameters` echo still reports a `time_range`** (doc gap): on 56
  searches with our `start_date`/`end_date`, the echo said `time_range` w 47, d 8, y 1 and held a start or end date
  in 0 of them, while 532 of 532 dated results fell inside our window.
  *Suggested change:* echo `start_date`/`end_date` when dates are sent. *Evidence:* `v2/ablation/arm_Td_*.json`.
- Map's silent empty answer (unexplained) on 5 of 5 official crawl-list sites and
  3 of 7 dairy sites (no error, no `failed_results`).
- On one scanned dairy rate-list PDF, Extract returned the letterhead but not the image-only rates (doc gap).
- `/usage` lag (doc gap): 6 credits on `/usage` against 226 from per-call
  `include_usage`, the same day.

## Feedback by product: Nebius Token Factory, Nemotron Nano, Nemotron Super (and Tavily, separately)
Each product answers the organisers' five questions. Only facts already logged in `FEEDBACK_NOTES.md` (dated
entries below) or `results/feedback_evidence/`, plus Nebius's own retirement notice (`config/doc_citations.json`).

**Nebius Token Factory**

- *What we used it for:* the one OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`api.tokenfactory.nebius.com`) for every model call, through
  `shadow_cpi/nemotron.py`.
- *What worked well:* JSON-schema output worked on the opening call (`checks.py`, "[PASS] Nemotron JSON output"), so
  every answer is parsed, not guessed; the `/models` list served several Nemotron models behind the one endpoint, so
  roles are picked by name in `config/models.json`.
- *What needs work:* one read timeout and one connection reset each stopped a long run (our helper now retries
  timeouts, not resets); the `/models` list mixes naming styles (case, `3.5` vs `3_5`) and puts a vision model next
  to the text models; the Nemotron IDs we use are removed from Serverless on 9 Nov 2026 (Dedicated Endpoints
  unaffected), so a project that must run through judging has to switch models mid-way, which we pre-registered on
  27 Oct.
- *Onboarding, zero to hello world:* key in `.env`, any OpenAI-compatible client pointed at the endpoint, `/models`,
  then one chat completion with a JSON schema: that is `checks.py`, and it passed on the opening run. The step that
  took care was choosing model IDs from the `/models` list.
- *Would we build with it again?* Yes: strict schema output and two model sizes behind one endpoint let code, not
  the model, decide every number. We would ask for retries on resets and a longer runway before retirements.

**NVIDIA Nemotron Nano** (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B`)

- *What we used it for:* the yes/no gatekeeper ("does this page state an Indian price or price change?") and
  display-only English glosses.
- *What worked well:* it answered the opening JSON-schema check in the requested shape.
- *What needs work:* it said "no" to a page that plainly listed rupee prices (a Delhi vegetable-price page); we added
  a code backstop so a page with a visible rupee price is never skipped.
- *Onboarding:* the same `checks.py` call; nothing model-specific to set up.
- *Would we build with it again?* Yes, as a cheap gatekeeper, with the code backstop in place.

**NVIDIA Nemotron Super** (`nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`)

- *What we used it for:* reading each page as numbered lines and citing the line for every price and price change;
  writing the search fields in arms B, C and H.
- *What worked well:* citing line numbers instead of copying text made Hindi pages work; the Hindi quotes that failed
  the code check were mostly prices written in words, which code cannot verify as numerals.
- *What needs work:* it sometimes labelled the item from the page's context rather than the cited line, took the low
  end of a price range, or took the old price in "from X to Y" sentences; code now requires the item name in the
  cited line, takes the midpoint of a range and reads "from X to Y" as a change.
- *Onboarding:* the `checks.py` price-extraction check (a numbered line cited, the number checked by code) passed on
  the opening run.
- *Would we build with it again?* Yes: line-number citing is what lets code check every number on the page.

**Tavily** (separate from Nebius and NVIDIA; the field notes are in `docs/tavily_bug_reports.md`)

- *What we used it for:* the news and price pages the evidence pipeline reads go through Tavily: Search with dates,
  Extract, Map and Crawl (endpoints used: `/search`, `/extract`, `/map`, `/crawl`). The exceptions are fetched directly and logged as
  service `direct` in the Flight Recorder: the official data (the MoSPI API and the Department of Consumer Affairs
  download), Wayback lookups, and the pages Tavily could not fetch, which `extract_or_download` retries as a direct,
  logged download.
- *What worked well:* dated news searches stayed inside the requested month in English and Hindi on the opening
  checks; the date fields held in Hindi, Marathi and Tamil; Extract read the MoSPI press-release PDF and IBJA's daily
  bullion PDFs; Crawl read DERC's tariff-order table; empty Map/Crawl calls were not charged, and a bad start address
  got a clear error.
- *What needs work:* Extract cannot read reuters.com or script-rendered data pages; Map returned nothing on several
  government and dairy sites with no error, and its `limit` cut off the newest pages; `/usage` did not update all
  day; `include_domains_mode="prefer"` let off-target results through; the Research endpoint has no date parameter;
  Extract has no as-of / crawl-timestamp field.
- *Onboarding:* key in `.env`, then the `checks.py` news search for a past month inside a date window, which passed
  on the opening run.
- *Would we build with it again?* Yes: explicit date windows are what kept later articles out of a historical
  search, and the date fields held in every language we tried.

## Accessibility
Every app page is checked in a real browser by `tools/check_contrast.py` (Chromium through Playwright): 15
pages, at 1440 and 390 px wide, in the light and the dark theme, measuring every visible text element against its
background for at least 4.5:1 (large text 3.0:1) and checking for horizontal overflow. Last run
29 Oct 2026: 0 elements below the threshold and 0 pages with overflow
(`docs/contrast_check.json`). It does not read text drawn inside charts or inside closed expanders. The theme's own
colour pairs are also tested at 4.5:1 without a browser (`tests/test_aesthetic.py`), and animation is switched
off under `prefers-reduced-motion` (`tests/test_aesthetic.py::test_reduced_motion_rule_and_viewer_toolbar`).

## Inspiration
India's CPI arrives about 12 days after the month ends. Forecasting it from the web means replaying past
months, and a replay that reads a page published after its cutoff looks better than it could ever be live. El Lahib et
al. (2026, arXiv 2602.00758) found at least one retrieved page containing major post-cutoff leakage for
71% of Google-audited questions, after 10–20 queries and about 100 URLs each; our 9/20
on the pre-registered initial pass (10/20 after the logged archive retry) is per search task, so the rates are not directly comparable. So we built a nowcast that tests, rather than assumes,
Tavily's date controls and measures what they cost.

## Related work
Shadow CPI is a pre-registered measurement of an agent-native search API's date controls, plus a shipped fix for the gap it found (time-locked search and an as-of page reader). Related studies, each checked on its arXiv page:

- **El Lahib et al. 2026**: "Temporal Leakage in Search-Engine Date-Filtered Web Retrieval: A Retrospective Forecasting Case Study": audits post-cutoff leakage in Google and DuckDuckGo date-filtered retrieval for forecasting questions (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00758).
- **OracleProto (Ma et al. 2026)**: a reproducible framework for benchmarking LLM forecasting via knowledge cutoffs and temporal masking (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03762).
- **LiveMacroEval (Zhao et al. 2026)**: "Can LLMs Take the Pulse of the Economy?": live LLM nowcasts of 16 US macro indicators (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30110).
- **Paleka, Goel, Geiping and Tramèr 2025**: "Pitfalls in Evaluating Language Model Forecasters": temporal leakage as a reason to distrust forecasting evaluations (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.00723).
- **Zhang and Stadie 2026**: "Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores": leakage from model memory, measured against a known training cutoff and a matched clean control (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02985).

## How it works
1. **Tavily Search proposes** pages, every call with `start_date`/`end_date` (the later time-locked searches also send
   `filter_by_published_date`; v1's frozen search used the dates plus our page-date check); code re-checks each date.
2. **Tavily Extract reads the page:** the model returns a line number; code copies that line from the Extract output
   and checks the number is in it. A model never writes a quote.
3. **Plain code computes:** index levels combined with MoSPI's official weights; year-on-year last.
4. **The seal:** canonical JSON + `SHA-256` + a git tag. We publish the prediction's SHA-256 and a Git tag before
   release, so anyone can verify the file they have. The seal proves when the forecast was
   committed, not what was read before it; the time lock and `extract_as_of` address the evidence.

**How we use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory:** a model reads and cites; code decides every number.
- **Nemotron Nano** (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B`; from 9 Nov 2026 `nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning`) is the yes/no gatekeeper: it screens each page for
  whether it is worth reading, and writes display-only English glosses. 622 calls sent (4,829
  including cache hits), median latency 1.3 s per call sent (`results/app/flight_recorder.jsonl`).
- **Nemotron Super** (`nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`; from 9 Nov 2026 `nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL`) reads the screened pages, cites the exact
  numbered line for each price or price change, and writes the search fields in arms B, C and H. 719 calls sent
  (5,177 including cache hits), median latency 2.3 s per call sent (same file).
- **Code** copies the cited line from Tavily's Extract output and checks that the number is in it; a model never writes
  a quote or chooses a number. The flight recorder does not log token counts, so none are reported.

Nebius retires the original IDs on 9 Nov 2026; from then, calls use Nebius's recommended replacements (pre-registered on 27 Oct).
Where Token Factory helped (dated entries in `FEEDBACK_NOTES.md`): JSON-schema output worked on the opening call;
the `/models` list served both sizes behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so roles are picked by name in config; and
having Super cite line numbers instead of copying text made Hindi pages work.

## What it does
- **The October 2026 nowcast.** Sealed on 29 Oct (tag `seal-2026-10`). October 2026 CPI is scheduled for 12 Nov at 4 pm IST (MoSPI's
  next-working-day rule applies).
  Sealed 29 Oct 2026, 09:32 IST: headline 6.090% year on year, 80% range 5.806–6.373%, P(≥6.0%) 0.66.
  Anyone can recompute the seal's `SHA-256` (`2d1dbc1dbb825e19b03d3f2dc5d555b25d3f1f81a5142d5effcbbb26732f0de7`) from the file at tag `seal-2026-10` (`verify.md`).
- **What Tavily added to the sealed estimate** (`tavily_attribution` in `sealed/2026-10.json`: the same code run with
  government price series only, against the full run with Tavily's evidence): with Tavily evidence the sealed
  October 2026 estimate is 6.090%; without it, 6.202%. The 12 Nov release will show
  whether it helped.
- **Price Shock Radar** (exploratory, report only): announced price changes taking effect this month;
  3 verified so far, 0 corroborated.
- **Live build** with **Replay a saved run** (no API call, no credits).
- **Chain of custody** from any number to its quote, page, Tavily request ID, response hash and seal; **`as_of()`**
  shows what was known on a past day.

## Reuse
`timelock/` (time-locked search, standard library only), `mcp/` (the same as an MCP tool), the benchmark
`benchmarks/timelock34/` (34 cases, 32 distinct questions (two pairs share a question and its
searches); new URLs a search returns are unlabelled until reviewed and are never counted as safe), `shadow_cpi/pit` (`pit_search(query, cutoff)`) and the agent skill `skills/time-locked-search/SKILL.md`. **For
research teams:** designed for event studies and backtests that must not see the outcome early; research tool, not
investment advice.

## Scoreboard
Jan–Sep 2026 replay, pre-registered, with one disclosed post-scoring correction (0.185 → 0.194;
`results/score_lock.json`): Shadow CPI v1 0.194 pp mean miss,
trend only 0.212, repeat-last-month 0.468. On the 6 poll months: 0.150 vs the
poll's 0.148, about a tie. The 80% range held in 5 of 9 months. v2 was not
better (0.206).

## Honest limits
14%–21% of the basket measured each month; recall 6 of 29; small,
India-focused samples with Wilson intervals (20 date-test cases and 14 finance events show the effect
exists and its size here, not Tavily's behaviour in general); data vintage: MoSPI began publishing the 2024-base
series (with its 2025 history) on 12 Feb 2026, so a real January 2026 nowcast could not
have used that history, while our January replay did (from February on it was public before
each nowcast); every case whose label changed after the archive retry (9 of 34) is listed
in `docs/retry_reconciliation.md`; 46 of 110 custody entries have both a request_id and a
response hash (later arms only); direct non-Tavily sources (MoSPI API, Department of Consumer Affairs (DoCA) download,
Wayback lookups); quote check (AI-assisted audit; pages then opened in a browser) 10 verbatim,
1 paywalled, 1 not checked; web news quotes ran in full only for March 2026; searches
start 10 days before the month, and v1's replay ran to month-end while the live seal stops at the
29th; v1 used `start_date`/`end_date` plus our own page-date check, and `filter_by_published_date` came later
(date test, radar, `timelock/`); an Uttar Pradesh (UP) electricity surcharge that may have been put on hold is left in
the score; a value-of-information score was dropped rather than tuned.
A Hindi substring match ('rail' inside 'domestic') turned a Jharkhand power tariff into a 'Bihar rail' event. Our
manual check caught it; the fix (whole-word matching, state from the page) removed the event, so the October radar
has 3 events. Logged as rule changes `R2`–`R3`, with before and after.
Exploratory and post-hoc results are labelled where they appear and changed no scored verdict.
**Model memory:** the time lock controls what search returns, not what the models know. NVIDIA's model cards
(checked 29 Oct 2026): Nemotron Nano pre-training 25 Jun 2025, post-training 28 Nov 2025; Nemotron Super
pre-training June 2025, post-training February 2026, inside the Jan–Sep 2026 replay; replacement models:
`nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning`: not published (no public model card found); `nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL`: not published (no public model card found). So the replay is not leakage-free against model memory; the sealed forward forecasts are the
clean evidence. Every zero is reported as zero detected, with its Wilson interval, and no-dates counts are lower bounds (absence
from Wayback is not proof a page did not exist).

## Testing instructions
1. **One minute, no key:** open the app's Leak demo (the opening screen: saved results, no API call), then the Field
   Report page for the full tables. Nothing is spent.
2. **Try it page, live on our credits:** ask a question with a cutoff; each run is two basic Tavily searches
   (2 credits), at most 3 runs per visit and 25 credits a day for the page. A
   repeat of the same question and cutoff within 24 hours is answered from that cached run for free. With
   no key the page shows a saved example; at the cap it says so and points to the Colab notebook.
3. **With your own Tavily key:** the Colab notebook (`notebooks/reproduce_leak.ipynb`, badge in the README) re-runs
   the leak check, and `repro/` holds one-request scripts for each field note. **Locally:** `pip install -r
   requirements-app.txt`, `streamlit run app.py` (no keys needed), `python -m pytest -q` (no keys, no credits).

## After the deadline
- **12 Nov, 4 pm IST:** MoSPI publishes October 2026 CPI; we score the sealed nowcast against
  it with `score.py`, and the Archive page shows the miss and whether the figure was inside the range.
- **9 Nov 2026:** the dated model switch; calls from that day use Nebius's replacement models, logged per call.
- **About 1 Dec:** the November seal, made with the replacement models and saying so.
